summary.headline: Kajaria Q2 FY27: volumes up 10% YoY, consolidated revenue up 24% to INR1,468 crore, EBITDA margin 19.5%, guided to stay around current levels.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 24% YoY to INR1,468 crore on 10% volume growth and price hikes taken in North and South plants (12-13%) and at Morbi (18-19%). EBITDA margin was 19.5% versus 17.94% a year earlier, and PAT rose to INR190 crore from INR133 crore. Management said export demand stayed subdued on freight and container constraints, while gas costs stayed high and are expected to remain tight. Management guided to double-digit volume growth over the next two quarters, stable margins, and new GVT capacity at Srikalahasti and Gailpur, with no further price hikes planned for now.

segments.name: Tiles
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,291 crore, up 23% YoY; volume growth reported across all regions and end-user segments (retail and project). Gas cost averaged about INR70/SCM in Q2 (North ~INR70.56, South INR63, West INR75).

segments.name: Bathware
segments.commentary: Revenue INR124 crore, up 22% YoY. Margin is currently low because the new plant is under-utilised; management expects it to approach tile margins next year. Sanitary and faucet growth of 21% split about 50% price and 50% volume.

segments.name: Adhesives
segments.commentary: Revenue INR54 crore, up 69% YoY. FY26 revenue was about INR125 crore and FY27 is guided to about INR240 crore, with about INR400 crore targeted next year. Expansion is 9,000 MT with peak revenue of about INR60-65 crore on a 12-hour shift.

segments.name: Subsidiary and JV tiles
segments.commentary: Realisation dipped slightly QoQ, which management attributed to a volume-led mix. Nepal JV (5 MSM capacity, about 85% utilisation) is equity-accounted and contributed about INR2.5 crore as income from associates.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth guided at double digits for the next two quarters (remaining 9 months of FY27 target of about 10%).
FY27 tile sales target about 130 MSM against 88 MSM own capacity; about 42 MSM to be outsourced from Morbi.
FY28 sales target about 145 MSM; capacity additions of about 22.5 MSM to bring own capacity to about 90-110 MSM, reducing outsourcing to about 36-37 MSM.
FY28 value growth expected to be modest because tile volume growth will be roughly equal to value growth; Bathware and adhesives expected to drive revenue growth.
EBITDA margin guided to stay around 19% with no price hikes planned; management prioritises absolute EBITDA over percentage margin.
Other expenses to stay at about INR138 crore per quarter due to higher advertising; employee cost guided at INR141-142 crore per quarter.
capex_capacity: Srikalahasti brownfield expansion raised to 12.5 MSM from 10 MSM; not yet commissioned and expected by end-June 2027. Capex rose to about INR240 crore from INR210 crore, mainly for a larger shed and warehouse; machinery cost up about 25%.
Gailpur expansion of 11 MSM on track; both new plants are 100% GVT and use about 30% biofuel in North.
Shed at Srikalahasti can be doubled to about 25 MSM with machinery-only capex later.
Nepal JV: 5 MSM capacity (mixed ceramic and GVT, from around Sept 2024) running at about 85% utilisation; total investment about INR200 crore.
Total installed capacity about 88 MSM (own plus JV) against Q2 production of 22.9 MSM versus 20.7 MSM stated capacity.
demand_pricing: Industry context: Morbi exports are expected at about INR12,000 crore for FY27 due to container costs; domestic industry about INR48,000 crore; total about INR60,000 crore.
Morbi gas prices rose from about INR50 on 28 Feb to about INR91 per SCM. Morbi players took about 35-40% price hikes versus 12-13% for Kajaria North and South plants.
Gap between Kajaria and Morbi dealer pricing narrowed from about 40% pre-28 Feb to about 20-25%.
Propane is now only about 5% cheaper than gas after rising in recent days; Brent is about $116 and management expects propane to rise further over the next 15 days.
Management estimates market growth at 5-6%, with the rest from share gains. About 40-50% of Morbi's 400-500 plants are not operating.

qa_highlights.question: What price hikes were taken and how much is year-to-date?
qa_highlights.answer: North and South plants raised prices about 12-13% across ceramic, PVT and GVT; Morbi about 18-19%. These are cumulative hikes to date, not Q2 only. Management said no price hike was taken in Q2 and none is planned for Q3 at present.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gas cost outlook and are price hikes needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Average gas cost in Q2 was about INR70/SCM (North ~INR70.56, South INR63, West INR75). Management expects a cost increase in Q3 for West, but targets a significant reduction from January through shorter firing cycles and cheaper sourcing. No further end-product price hikes are needed for now.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Srikalahasti capex increase and why are they adding capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity was raised to 12.5 MSM from 10 MSM, with capex rising to about INR240 crore from INR210 crore due to a larger shed and warehouse. Expansion is intended to support double-digit volume growth and gas advantage over Morbi.

qa_highlights.question: Will volume growth dilute margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said blended margin will remain around current levels. Future margin gains are expected from operating leverage, lower freight costs, and cheaper GVT capacity, but management is not guiding above about 19%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses and borrowing change?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses at INR138 crore are expected to stay at this level due to higher advertising. Management said borrowings were working-capital draws, partly to fund JV bank limits, and treasury loans of about INR155 crore went to NBFCs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the adhesives and bathware businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: Adhesives revenue is guided to about INR240 crore in FY27 and about INR400 crore next year. Bathware margin is low now but should approach tile margins next year.

risks_watch: Gas and propane costs are rising; spot gas is about $28-30/SCM and management has no visibility on a decline in gas prices.
Export demand is subdued because of freight and container constraints.
Srikalahasti expansion is not commissioned until end-June 2027; capex overrun is a watch item.
Bathware margin is low due to under-utilisation; adhesives expansion execution is a watch item.
Treasury deployments of about INR155 crore into NBFCs and JV-related borrowing of about INR178 crore need monitoring.
Management did not disclose cost per SCM for Nepal and only said it would respond later.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes, share gains and margins, but cautious on gas costs and export demand. Management was evasive on FY28 value growth, Nepal gas cost and specific treasury counterparties.
